enterprise:
StackVitals has no server and no account: it runs in your GitHub Actions with your tokens and keeps everything in your
repos. So the controls an enterprise asks a vendor for are GitHub's own, applied to StackVitals like to any workflow.

| What you need | Where it comes from | What to set |
|---|---|---|
| Single sign-on | Your GitHub organization's SAML or OIDC SSO | Nothing extra: people reach the app and the data through GitHub. A personal token a person pastes into the app must be SSO-authorized like any other. |
| Who can see what | Repository permissions | The data branch and the app have the repo's visibility. Private repos' pages stay private (Enterprise Cloud private Pages) or aren't published at all (`pages: artifact`). The Portal leaves private repos out of every page a public portal repo writes. |
| Who can change what | Repository roles | Settings changes need write access to the repo, decisions triage access, golden paths write access to the portal repo and to the target repo; the workflow starts only for owners, members and collaborators ([threat-model.md](threat-model.md)). |
| Audit log | GitHub's audit log, plus StackVitals' own | Every decision and settings change is appended to `decisions/log.ndjson` on the data branch with who, when, why and from where; the app's Activity page shows it. GitHub's audit log records the workflow runs and token use. |
| Data residency | Where your GitHub data lives | StackVitals' history is files in your repo, so it stays wherever your GitHub Enterprise data resides. What leaves the repo, and how to keep it all inside GitHub, is on [privacy.md](privacy.md). |
| Secrets | GitHub Actions secrets | Keys live in your repo's or org's secrets and reach only their own service's host ([privacy.md](privacy.md)). |
| Supply chain | Pinned actions, signed releases | Every action StackVitals' own workflows use is pinned to a commit; pin the StackVitals Action itself to a release's commit SHA rather than `@v0`. The release workflow signs each release with Sigstore and adds an SBOM and build provenance ([SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md)). |
| Uptime and support | GitHub Actions' availability | There is no StackVitals service to go down: a missed run is caught up by the next one. There is no paid SLA; report problems as issues, and security problems privately ([SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md)). |
| Certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001) | GitHub's | StackVitals has no service of its own, so GitHub's certifications cover where the data lives. By default the dependency check sends package names to deps.dev and the registries; `[deps] outside_lookups = false` stops that ([privacy.md](privacy.md)). The code is open to review. |

## Rate limits on Enterprise Cloud

The workflow token allows 15,000 requests an hour on Enterprise Cloud (1,000 elsewhere). The busiest public repos need
under 40% of the smaller limit for CI Health ([bench/accuracy/platform](../bench/accuracy/platform/README.md)).
privacy:
StackVitals runs in your own workflow and keeps its history in your repo. There is no StackVitals server: nothing is sent to us. This page lists everything a run (or the app) sends anywhere, built from the code's own list, and a test fails if the code gains an outside host this page doesn't name.

| Feature | Goes to | What is sent | When | To turn it off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Every module (reading your repo, writing its results) | api.github.com, github.com | Requests with the workflow's own token: it reads runs, logs, pull requests, issues and files of this repo, and writes the stackvitals-data branch, Pages, and the comments, labels and issues your switches allow. | every run | Stays inside GitHub; remove a module from `modules` to stop it. |
| Delivery from Bitbucket or Azure DevOps (command line) | api.bitbucket.org, dev.azure.com | Read-only requests for the repo you name, with BITBUCKET_TOKEN or AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN when set; nothing about a GitHub repo. | only when you run `stackvitals delivery --bitbucket` or `--azure` | Don't run it. |
| SonarQube or SonarCloud code quality | sonarcloud.io | The Sonar project key in [connectors.sonar] (and the SONAR_TOKEN when set), to read its quality gate and measures. | once a day, when a project is set | Leave project under [connectors.sonar] empty. |
| Security checks: the OpenSSF Best Practices badge | www.bestpractices.dev | A public repo's address, to look up its badge level; a private repo's is never sent. | once a week | Remove `deps` from `modules`. |
| Benchmarks from public repos | github.com | A download of the crawl's benchmark files from stackvitals/stackvitals's releases; nothing about your repo is sent. | every run, cached a day | Nothing to turn off: it is a download. |
| Shared benchmark figures (opt-in) | github.com | An issue on stackvitals/stackvitals, filed by a person from a link in the run summary: this repo's rounded CI figures, its language and star tier, a random id kept in the data branch, and its name only with `name = true`. It is public once filed, and shows the account that filed it. | only when someone files the link | `[benchmarks] share = false` (the default); close the issue to withdraw it. |
| Dependency licences and Scorecards | api.deps.dev, api.scorecard.dev | The name and version of every package in the dependency graph (to deps.dev; that includes the names of private or internal packages the graph lists) and the public source repos behind them (to OpenSSF Scorecard); never this repo's name. | weekly, Dependencies module | `[deps] outside_lookups = false`. |
| Known vulnerabilities in every lockfile | github.com, api.osv.dev, api.deps.dev, osv-vulnerabilities.storage.googleapis.com | A download of the pinned OSV-Scanner from its GitHub release (checked against its SHA-256); then the name and version of every package in the repo's lockfiles to OSV (and, for manifests without exact versions, to deps.dev to resolve them). With outside lookups off, OSV's public databases are downloaded instead and no package name is sent. | after CI runs and on the schedule, at most every 6 hours unless a lockfile changed; Dependencies module | `[deps] outside_lookups = false` (scans offline). |
| Release checks on changed packages | registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, api.deps.dev | The name and the old and new versions of each npm or PyPI package a pull request adds or upgrades (at most 30), to read when it was released, its install scripts, dependencies and build provenance. | pull requests that change a lockfile | `[deps] outside_lookups = false`. |
| Runtime versions | endoflife.date | Only the runtime's name (nodejs, python, php, ruby or go), to read its release lines and support dates; never the repo or its versions. | weekly, Dependencies module | `[deps] outside_lookups = false`. |
| GuardDog code check (opt-in) | pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, registry.npmjs.org | Downloads of GuardDog itself and of each npm or PyPI package version a pull request adds or upgrades (at most 10), whose code it reads on the runner; nothing about the repo is sent. | pull requests that change a lockfile, only with `[deps] guarddog = true` | Off by default. |
| History in a bucket (opt-in) | the s3-endpoint you set | Every file of the data branch (history, pages, decisions), signed with your bucket key, to your own bucket. | every run, only with `storage: s3://...` | The default, `storage: git`. |
| Look-alike package check | api.npmjs.org, pypistats.org | Only the name of a package a pull request adds whose name is one edit from a popular one, to read its weekly downloads. | pull requests that change a lockfile | `[deps] outside_lookups = false` (names are still checked). |
| Model triage of unexplained CI failures | api.anthropic.com, api.groq.com, api.mistral.ai, api.openai.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com, the `url` you set under [ci.triage] | The failing step's log excerpt (bounded) and the changed files' names, with your key, to the provider you choose or the endpoint you set; at most 3 calls a run. | off until `[ci.triage]` and a key are set; a private repo also needs `allow_private = true` | Off by default. |
| Issue trackers and incident tools | *.atlassian.net, api.linear.app, api.pagerduty.com, api.incident.io | Requests with your key that read issues, sprints and incidents; with write-back on, a comment linking the merged pull request (and a status move). | only with a key in the workflow; write-back only with `write_back = true` | Remove the key. |
| A Discourse forum | your forum's host | Read requests for its public topics, with no key; only times and flags are kept, never usernames or text. | only with url under [connectors.discourse] | Remove the url. |
| Slack and Discord support channels | slack.com, discord.com | Read requests with your bot token for the channels you name; only times and flags are kept, never text or user ids. | only with a slack-token or discord-token | Remove the token. |
| Copilot usage reports | api.github.com, the report file host GitHub names | Requests with the reports token; the report file is fetched without it. | only with the Copilot token | Remove the token. |
| AI spend | api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, api.cursor.com | Read-only cost and usage report requests, each with that provider's own admin key; nothing about the repo. | only with an AI spend admin key | Remove the key. |
| Chat alerts and the weekly digest | your webhook's host (Slack, Teams, Discord, other) | Alert and digest text: metric names and values, test names, this repo's name, links to its pages. | only with a webhook secret | Remove the webhook. |
| Test connection | each connector's own host (above), your webhook's host, the s3-endpoint you set, your model provider, your GitLab host (`CI_API_V4_URL`) | One cheap call per connector asked for, with its own key: it reads one item, never writes to a tracker. A chat webhook gets one labelled test message ("StackVitals connection test"), never retried; a bucket gets one small object (`.stackvitals-check`) written and deleted under the prefix; model triage calls the provider's model list; GitLab reads the project and the token's own scopes, at `CI_API_V4_URL` for a self-hosted GitLab. The results go in docs/connectors.json; on a public repo without account, channel, team or bucket names. | only when someone with write access presses Test connection, comments `/stackvitals check`, or runs `stackvitals connectors check` | Don't run it. |
| Exports (DevLake, CTRF, Postgres, OpenTelemetry) | api.github.com | Reads with your token; the files are written on your machine and sent nowhere. | only when you run `stackvitals export` | Don't run it. |
| Portal Scorecard checks | api.scorecard.dev | The names of the organisation's public repos; private repos are never sent. | weekly, Portal module | Leave the Portal module out. |
| GitLab CI | gitlab.com | Requests with your GitLab token for one project's pipelines and jobs. The GitLab job also writes the project's stackvitals-data branch, its Pages and one merge request note, and downloads StackVitals from github.com and its packages from PyPI. | when you run `stackvitals ci gitlab`, or each pipeline once you include the GitLab job | Don't run or include it. |
| The app in a viewer's browser | your Pages site, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, avatars.githubusercontent.com, api.linear.app, your sign-in relay (optional), cdn.jsdelivr.net, cdnjs.cloudflare.com | The viewer's browser loads the app from your Pages site (its code, font and docs are all there). With a GitHub token or sign-in, the app calls api.github.com with it to read repos and data branches, set up the workflow, save settings and decisions, and save secrets sealed in the browser; workflow files and data are also read from raw.githubusercontent.com, and the account picture from avatars.githubusercontent.com. Testing a Linear key from the page sends it only to api.linear.app. Sign in with GitHub, when the site was built with a relay, sends the one-time code (and later the refresh token) to that relay, which swaps it for a token and keeps nothing. Explore loads DuckDB from jsDelivr; printable pages load Chart.js from cdnjs. Nothing goes to a server of ours. | when someone opens the app | Keep Pages private, or don't publish them; don't connect GitHub in the app. |

## Nothing leaves GitHub

Leave model triage, connectors and webhooks unset (they are, by default), and set `[deps] outside_lookups = false`. Runs then talk to GitHub only: your repo, and the benchmark download from public releases. A private repo's Pages are private on plans that allow it; otherwise publish none and read the job summary and the data branch.

## What each token can reach

- **The workflow token** (`GITHUB_TOKEN`): this repo only, with the permissions the workflow file grants.
- **An optional personal or App token** (`stackvitals-token`): whatever it was granted; the Portal's App is read-only.
- **Tracker and incident keys:** only their own service's host; the Jira key goes only to an `*.atlassian.net` site.
- **A model key:** its provider's host, or the `url` you set under `[ci.triage]`.
threat-model:
StackVitals runs inside your own GitHub Actions with your repo's tokens, reads text that strangers write (pull request
titles, test names, logs, issues, comments) and writes back to GitHub (comments, labels, issues, the data branch). This
page lists what could go wrong, what stops it, and the committed test that fails if the protection breaks
(`tests/test_flow_*.py`; a test below that no longer exists fails `test_the_threat_model_names_only_tests_that_exist`).
What leaves the repo is listed separately in [privacy.md](privacy.md); how to report a problem is in
[SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).

## Untrusted input

| Threat | What stops it | Test |
|---|---|---|
| A fork PR's test or job name pings people or plants a link in a comment, issue or chat message | Names are code-formatted, `@` and links are neutralised, chat payloads are escaped | `test_real_logs_keep_to_the_failing_step_and_comments_cannot_ping_or_link`, `test_a_flaky_test_name_never_becomes_a_chat_link_or_ping`, `test_preflight_note_cannot_ping_people_or_make_links` |
| A job or PR name injects markup into the pages | Every page escapes repo text | `test_dashboard_and_summary_escape_job_names_from_untrusted_workflows`, `test_pr_titles_from_strangers_are_escaped` |
| A test report is a zip or XML bomb | Size limits, in-memory reads, defusedxml | `test_hostile_xml_is_refused_without_crashing`, `test_oversized_artifacts_are_skipped_not_downloaded`, `test_every_report_format_reads_into_one_shape_and_hostile_xml_is_refused` |
| A failing log tells a model (triage, or an agent using the MCP server) what to do | CI text is fenced and labelled as data | `test_the_ai_prompt_fences_ci_text_so_an_agent_never_obeys_it` |
| A fork PR's test report claims a real test passed on retry, so it gets called known flaky, re-run or quarantined | Fork runs' flaky and coverage claims are dropped; their failures still show on their own PR | `test_a_fork_report_cannot_mark_a_test_flaky_or_set_coverage` |
| A pull request's own lockfile or manifest misleads or breaks the dependency check | The PR's code is never run, files are parsed with limits, the check never fails the PR | `test_the_pr_check_cannot_be_fooled_or_broken_by_the_prs_own_files` |

## Fork pull requests and `workflow_run`

| Threat | What stops it | Test |
|---|---|---|
| A fork PR's workflow runs with write tokens | StackVitals starts from `workflow_run` after CI, in the base repo's context, and reads the fork's results as data: it never checks out or runs the PR's code | `test_fork_runs_join_the_pr_that_was_open_on_that_branch_at_the_time`, `test_a_fork_pr_is_found_and_the_comment_is_edited_not_reposted` |
| A fork PR gets a deps comment or a write | The lockfile check comments only on same-repo PRs | `test_the_pr_check_reads_lockfile_changes_and_never_comments_on_forks` |

**Triggers.** The workflow `stackvitals ci init` writes starts on `workflow_run` (after your CI finishes), a schedule,
`workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch` (deployments and incidents sent with `stackvitals record`, which
needs a token that can write to the repo), a push that changes its settings or workflow file, `issues` and `issue_comment` (commands and app
requests, checked against the sender's permission), and `pull_request` only when a lockfile changes. It never uses
`pull_request_target`. On a fork's pull request GitHub gives that `pull_request` run a read-only token and no secrets,
and StackVitals reads the lockfiles through the API without checking out or running the PR's code. The Portal's
workflow starts on a schedule, `workflow_dispatch`, `issues` and `issue_comment` (only `/stackvitals approve` from
owners, members and collaborators starts a runner; the job checks both people's write access, refuses self-approval,
and runs only the request text the approval's code names).

| Threat | What stops it | Test |
|---|---|---|
| A workflow runs the base repo's token and secrets on a fork's code (`pull_request_target`) | No workflow StackVitals writes or ships uses that trigger | `test_no_workflow_uses_pull_request_target` |

## Who can change things

| Threat | What stops it | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Anyone opening an issue or commenting changes settings or decisions | The workflow starts only for owners, members and collaborators; the job checks write access for settings and triage access for decisions | `test_a_request_changes_settings_only_for_someone_with_write_access`, `test_a_comment_command_is_logged_and_reaches_the_quarantine_list` |
| A golden path writes to a repo its requester can't | The org App checks the requester's write access to the target repo first | `test_a_golden_path_never_writes_to_a_repo_the_requester_cannot_write_to` |

## Keys and tokens

| Threat | What stops it | Test |
|---|---|---|
| A tracker key is sent to a host an attacker names in settings | The Jira site must be `*.atlassian.net`, redirects aren't followed, keys go only to their service's own host. The one exception is the triage key: it goes to the https endpoint set in `[ci.triage] url` in the repo's own settings file, which only people with write access can change | `test_the_jira_key_can_only_go_to_an_atlassian_site_even_through_an_app_request`, `test_the_copilot_key_never_reaches_the_report_file_host` |
| A refused key's text ends up in a page or summary | Errors say what was refused, never the key | `test_a_refused_key_is_said_without_the_key_and_keeps_what_was_pulled` |
| A workflow runs code from a moved tag | Every action StackVitals' own workflows and the Action use is pinned to a commit (the Action itself is yours to pin; see below) | `test_every_action_is_pinned_to_a_commit` |
| A new upload to PyPI changes what the Action runs with your token and secrets | The Action installs from its `uv.lock`: exact versions with hashes, never the newest, and only the 11 packages it needs, not the 37 of a full install with the MCP server | `test_the_action_installs_its_locked_dependencies` |
| A compromised build tool changes a release before it is signed | The build job is read-only with a pinned build backend and no cache; a separate job, behind the `release` environment, signs and publishes | `test_releases_build_read_only_and_sign_in_a_separate_job` |

## The app in the browser

| Threat | What stops it | Test |
|---|---|---|
| The app's page runs code from elsewhere | The app is bundled into the data branch (only Explore and the printable module pages load DuckDB and Chart.js from jsDelivr, at pinned versions); the page allows only its own scripts (`script-src 'self'`) and talks only to GitHub's API and raw files, other repos' Pages sites (`*.github.io`, to read a public repo's published data), Linear's API and the optional sign-in relay; images load only from itself and GitHub's avatar host (`avatars.githubusercontent.com`) | `test_the_app_ships_with_its_libraries_licences_and_no_remote_code` |
| A GitHub token pasted in the app outlives the visit | It stays in the tab's session storage and is gone when the tab closes, unless the person ticks "Remember on this device"; Sign out removes it. It goes only to `api.github.com`. On an `<owner>.github.io` Pages address, every Pages site of that owner shares one origin, so another of the owner's Pages sites opened in the same tab can read the tab's token ("Remember" is off there for the same reason) | |
| The sign-in relay keeps or leaks tokens | The relay is optional and stateless: it only swaps GitHub's one-time code (with PKCE and a state check) or a refresh token for a token and returns it; it stores nothing and serves only the app's own address | `nothing is logged`, `unknown origins, missing PKCE, foreign redirects and odd grants never reach GitHub` (worker/relay) |
| A connector secret saved from the app is seen on the way | The value is sealed in the browser (libsodium sealed box) with the repo's own Actions public key; only the sealed value reaches GitHub, and the app never reads a secret back | `a sealed secret opens with the repo's private key and holds the exact value` (web/test) |

## Private data on public pages

| Threat | What stops it | Test |
|---|---|---|
| A public repo's data branch keeps private tracker titles, links or sprint names | Titles, links and sprint names are dropped for public repos | `test_a_public_repo_never_keeps_tracker_titles_links_or_sprint_names` |
| A public portal shows private repos | Private repos are left out of every page and file | `test_private_repos_never_reach_a_public_page_and_forks_are_not_judged` |
| Code starts sending data to a new host without the privacy page saying so | Every outside host in the code must be on the privacy page | `test_the_privacy_page_names_every_outside_host_the_code_can_reach` |
| Dependency names leave a private repo | `[deps] outside_lookups = false` keeps every name in the repo | `test_with_outside_lookups_off_no_dependency_name_leaves_the_repo` |

## Losing or corrupting history

| Threat | What stops it | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Two runs overwrite each other's history | Pushes retry on top of the other run | `test_overlapping_runs_converge_without_losing_either_side` |
| A run dies half way and leaves partial data | Nothing is written until the commit; the next run catches up | `test_a_run_that_dies_before_its_commit_leaves_nothing_and_the_next_run_catches_up` |
| A write to Jira or Linear repeats when a push is retried | Write-back is planned before the commit and sent once after it | `test_write_back_sends_after_the_commit_once_and_never_floods_old_issues` |

## Not covered

- Your own workflow file: StackVitals can't stop someone with write access from editing it.
- The StackVitals Action reference in your workflow: `@v0` moves with each release. To fix exactly what runs, pin it to a
  release's commit SHA, as you would any action.
- GitHub itself, the runners and the actions it pins.
- What a model provider does with what triage sends it (off by default; [privacy.md](privacy.md)).
